tagline: A twelve-mile detour to the river town that lost the court.
intro: KY 524 leaves US 42 between Goshen and Sligo and comes back to it twelve miles on, having gone down to the Ohio River at Westport in between. Across the water is Indiana.

Westport had its day early. Steamboats and showboats called at its docks, and for a time it held the Oldham County court. Then the railroad passed it by, the river trade fell off, and the flood of 1884 took 27 buildings. About 250 people live there now, and their post office has been open since 1815.

moments.title: Westport landing
moments.text: Levi Bowyer ran a ferry from here to the Indiana shore as early as 1800, and by 1818 the town was a commercial center where steamboats stopped regularly.

moments.title: Old Westport Courthouse
moments.text: The Westport Methodist Church was built as the county courthouse, and the court left it in 1838 for La Grange, which won the vote with a railroad on its way.
